# Canonical JSON Tool Contract

[1] list_dir
runtime_name: ls
aliases: ls
read_only: true
parallel_safe: true
description: List files in a directory.
examples:
- {"tool":"list_dir","args":{"path":"."}}

[2] read_file
runtime_name: read
aliases: read
read_only: true
parallel_safe: true
description: Read one file. Large files are returned in complete-line pages. In CodeMode, value is an object: value.text is the page text (a string), with start_line, end_line, total_lines, next_offset and text_complete metadata.
examples:
- {"tool":"read_file","args":{"path":"app.py"}}
- {"tool":"read_file","args":{"path":"app.py","offset":301,"limit":300}}

[3] read_files
runtime_name: -
aliases: -
read_only: true
parallel_safe: false
description: Read up to 8 files in one step. Do not nest it inside parallel.
examples:
- {"tool":"read_files","args":{"paths":["a.py","b.py"]}}

[4] grep
runtime_name: search
aliases: search
read_only: true
parallel_safe: true
description: Search file contents for literal text before reading when the location is unknown. Uses packaged ripgrep. Defaults to literal, case-insensitive matching; set literal=false for regex, case_sensitive=true for exact case, include for one positive glob, exclude for positive globs to omit, and before_context/after_context for surrounding lines. Use rg braces for alternatives, e.g. include='*.{py,ts}'; comma-separated globs are not alternatives. Globs are relative to the workspace root even when path narrows the search. Exclude directories with an array such as exclude=['src/vendor/**']. Searches hidden and ignored files within the admitted workspace scope, excluding build/VCS directories and symlinks. CodeMode value is a page object with matches and explicit coverage; column_byte is one-based UTF-8 bytes. Read matched files for context.
examples:
- {"tool":"grep","args":{"query":"login handler","path":"."}}
- {"tool":"grep","args":{"query":"TODO","path":"src","include":"*.{py,ts}","exclude":["src/vendor/**"]}}

[5] find_references
runtime_name: references
aliases: references
read_only: true
parallel_safe: false
description: Find bounded lexical reference hints for a simple symbol. This is not semantic resolution; use read_file before editing.
examples:
- {"tool":"find_references","args":{"symbol":"createRouter","path":"."}}

[6] workspace_diff
runtime_name: workspace_diff
aliases: -
read_only: true
parallel_safe: false
description: Compare this task's written files to their original snapshots. Reports external changes and the current task diff.
examples:
- {"tool":"workspace_diff","args":{}}

[7] semantic_definition
runtime_name: semantic_definition
aliases: -
read_only: true
parallel_safe: false
description: Query an installed Python, JS/TS, Go or Rust language server. operation defaults to definition; references, hover, diagnostics, documentSymbol and rename are read-only queries. Rename returns a version-bound plan. CodeMode application: const receipt=await tools.semantic_definition(inputs); return unwrap(await tools.edit({semantic_result_ref:receipt.result_ref})); Keep the OUTER receipt; do not unwrap it before reading result_ref. Never copy or reconstruct the replacement text. Push diagnostics are observations, not a complete verification.
examples:
- {"tool":"semantic_definition","args":{"path":"app.py","line":12,"symbol":"run"}}

[8] syntax_query
runtime_name: syntax_query
aliases: -
read_only: true
parallel_safe: false
description: Find bounded syntax nodes in Python or JS/TS. node_type is a grammar node such as FunctionDef, function_declaration, call_expression or import_statement. Returns file version and line ranges, not permission to edit.
examples:
- {"tool":"syntax_query","args":{"path":"app.ts","node_type":"function_declaration"}}

[9] parallel
runtime_name: -
aliases: -
read_only: true
parallel_safe: false
description: Batch at most 4 independent read-only list_dir, read_file, or grep calls. Local results are returned in request order.
examples:
- {"tool":"parallel","args":{"calls":[{"tool":"grep","args":{"query":"login","path":"."}},{"tool":"list_dir","args":{"path":"."}}]}}

[10] edit
runtime_name: edit
aliases: -
read_only: false
parallel_safe: false
description: Edit existing files with up to 8 exact replacements, preserving unrelated code. For replacements, omit content and base_result_ref. For a Python definition, use symbol and content. Create new files with content. For a whole-file update, use content plus base_result_ref. base_result_ref must be a complete read_file receipt from this task; changed versions are rejected. Copy old_string exactly, including indentation and whitespace. Include surrounding lines and the target text together in old_string of the same replacement so it matches one location uniquely. Preserve those surrounding lines in new_string. Separate replacement objects do not scope one another. Use the returned current context to refine the replacement; if insufficient, reread the file. Do not repeat the failed search unchanged. For a difficult multiline change, use content with the complete read_file base_result_ref, preserving unrelated text.
examples:
- {"tool":"edit","args":{"path":"app.py","replacements":[{"old_string":"def process():\n    return old_value\n","new_string":"def process():\n    return new_value\n"}]}}
- {"tool":"edit","args":{"path":"new_app.py","content":"full file contents"}}
- {"tool":"edit","args":{"path":"app.py","replacements":[{"old_string":"old1","new_string":"new1"},{"old_string":"old2","new_string":"new2"}]}}

[11] run
runtime_name: run
aliases: -
read_only: false
parallel_safe: false
description: Run a test, build, lint, or check. Use output_tail_lines to limit displayed output instead of a shell pipe. Other commands request user approval when available.
examples:
- {"tool":"run","args":{"command":"python -m unittest","path":"."}}

[12] shell
runtime_name: shell
aliases: -
read_only: false
parallel_safe: false
description: Ask the user to approve a necessary non-allowlisted command.
examples:
- {"tool":"shell","args":{"command":"git status --short","path":"."}}

[13] done
runtime_name: -
aliases: -
read_only: false
parallel_safe: false
description: Finish the task. summary is the complete user-facing response. For discussion, explanation, or read-only analysis, answer directly instead of merely saying that the topic was discussed.
examples:
- {"tool":"done","args":{"summary":"direct final response to the user"}}

--- rendered prompt contract ---
  {"tool":"list_dir","args":{"path":"."}}
    List files in a directory.

  {"tool":"read_file","args":{"path":"app.py"}}
  {"tool":"read_file","args":{"path":"app.py","offset":301,"limit":300}}
